title: Bodhinyanarama Accounts
kicker: Wellington Theravada Buddhist Association · Bodhinyanarama Monastery · Stokes Valley, Lower Hutt, New Zealand
cpiName: the New Zealand consumer price index (World Bank; for a year to 31 March, the calendar year in which most of it falls)
costDefShort: total expenditure as the Association reports it, which includes wear on buildings (depreciation).
defs: Spending: the total expenditure the Association reports to the New Zealand Charities Register each year, which includes wear on buildings (depreciation); the register shows only this total. Residents: the monks, novices, nuns and anagārikas listed at Bodhinyanarama on the community lists, on average; guests and lay residents are not counted. Inflation: the New Zealand consumer price index (World Bank). All amounts in New Zealand dollars, as paid at the time, unless the page says "in today's money".
incomeNote: The register gives no reason for the high income in the year to March 2026.
meaningNote: The register gives only two totals a year, so this page cannot say what the money was spent on.
holdLede: The Association's own AGM minutes, published on the monastery's website, also give net assets for some years.
holdSub: Net assets at 31 March: everything the Association owns less everything it owes. The AGM minutes give them for 2014 to 2017, 2019 and 2021 only.
notes: Where the figures come from. The annual returns of the Wellington Theravada Buddhist Association Incorporated (charity CC29078) on the New Zealand Charities Register: total income and total expenditure for the years to 31 March 2017 to 2026 (register_returns.txt in this folder keeps the table). For 2014 to 2016 and for net assets the page uses the treasurer's reports in the Association's AGM minutes on the monastery's own website (bodhinyanarama.net.nz/history_agm).
Years. The Association's year runs from 1 April to 31 March and is named by the year it ends in: "2026" is April 2025 to March 2026.

Spending includes wear on buildings. The minutes report "income after depreciation", and income less that figure equals the register's expenditure (2017: $114,712 less $7,633 is $107,079; 2019: $168,800 less $74,610 is $94,190). Nothing is taken out, so the page cannot show running costs without depreciation.

2014 to 2016. The minutes give income and the net income after depreciation for these years; spending is income less that net income ($88,461, $79,651 and $94,300). The minutes also quote expenses of $32,230, $45,940 and $60,776 for those years, which leave out depreciation.

Net assets. From the minutes: $2,026,303 (2014), $2,065,143 (2015), $2,088,822 (2016), $2,096,208 (2017), about $2,303,117 (2019) and about $2,348,284 (2021). The register does not show assets, cash or a list of costs.
Income. The year to March 2026 shows $759,177, against $115,000 to $232,000 in the other years. The register does not say why.
Residents are the monks, novices, nuns and anagārikas on the community lists (the Vassa list in July and the Winter list of the next January). Guests, retreatants and lay residents are not counted.
sources: Sources anyone can check: the New Zealand Charities Register, Wellington Theravada Buddhist Association Incorporated (CC29078), and its AGM minutes. Residents: the monasteries' community lists. Updated __UPDATED__
